summary: One app for everyone who signs in. The event switcher at the top left lists all your events with your role in each, and the sidebar changes with that role.
Every role starts on a Home that says what to do now: one next step and the next deadline.

Organisers get eight focused sections: Overview, Event page, People, Teams, Entries, Judging, Results, Settings. Judging (setting up and running it) and Results (publishing) are now separate, so Publish never sits above an unfinished rubric.
Participants get Home, Schedule, Announcements, Team, Entry, Website and Results. The entry form is no longer buried under team management, and sections that are not open yet say when they open.
Judges get Home, Queue and Rubric & brief, and score in a full-focus view: the entry and its website on the left, the rubric on the right, every tap saved.
On a phone, participants and judges use a bottom tab bar; organisers get a menu.
Nothing new is invented: all 160 things Simple Hack does today have a home on a screen. Leave this event (SIM-340) is shown as planned.

shell.desktop: Built from the kit (kit.css + shell.js): a fixed left .side holds the event .switcher (colour mark + name + role, opens .menu-pop listing every event with role and stage), the .nav list for the current role (icon + label, .count badge at the right), and a .side-foot with Account and a persistent Help link (replays the role's walkthrough -- see decisions on organiser-overview and judge-rubric). The .content column carries a .status bar on every screen except where a screen opts out (stage .pill, next-action text, .grow spacer); organisers additionally get the full event .stages track under it on Overview. Work surfaces are calm and dense, Linear-like: .card blocks, .list rows, .field/.input forms, .setting rows with .toggle or .seg controls, .grid3/.stat tiles, .note callouts (info/warn/ok/bad), .danger-zone and .dialog for anything hard to undo. Paper #f4efdf, ink #2b2925, red accent #a33f31 for primary actions and danger, teal #216c6a for stage pills and progress bars. The hand font (wordmark class) is reserved for the Simple Hack wordmark only -- every heading and label is the system stack.
shell.phone: shell.js renders .phone-top (switcher + a Menu/More button) and, for participant and judge, a fixed .tabbar built from each role's phone_tab items (icon + short label + .count badge); organisers get no tabbar, only the Menu button, which opens the same .nav as a full-screen sheet (app.menu-open). A role's items not marked phone_tab live behind the tabbar's trailing More button as the same sheet. The .status bar collapses to one line under the phone top bar. Forms and lists go full width, single column; any screen with a bottom primary action (judge-scoring's Save & next, participant-entry's Save) pins it with .sticky-foot so it never scrolls out of reach.
shell.switcher: The .switcher button plus .menu-pop dropdown lists every event the person belongs to (P.events in the kit), each row: colour .ev-mark with its 2-letter short code, name, and 'Role · Stage' (e.g. 'Judge · Judging'). Rows needing attention sort first. 'All your events' and 'Find a hackathon' sit under a second 'More' label at the bottom of the pop-over, matching shell.js exactly. The full-page version of this same list is landing-your-events.
shell.status_header: Organiser: .pill.stage (teal dot + stage label) + the next-action sentence + the join/judge links' Copy actions, with the full .stages progress track (done/now states) directly under it on Overview only. Participant: .pill.stage + next-action text, and once Building has a deadline, a live .clock chip counting down. Judge: .pill.stage reading only Open or Locked (never a stage name a judge doesn't need) + one sentence of context -- the one thing the brief says a judge must never be unsure about.

organiser.title: Welcome to your event
organiser.body: This is Overview, your event’s home. It always says the next thing to do. Here is a one-minute look around.

organiser.title: Stage and next deadline
organiser.body: The stage and the next deadline are always shown here. The stage decides what participants and judges can do right now.

organiser.title: Move the event on
organiser.body: When you are ready, change the stage: open sign-up, start building, close entries, judging, results, then end. Each change says what will happen before you confirm.

organiser.title: Invite people
organiser.body: Send the join link to participants and the judge link to judges. New link stops the old one working, so use it only if a link leaked.

organiser.title: Event page
organiser.body: What visitors see before they sign up: description, dates, schedule, sponsors, FAQ and announcements. You can also put up your own website.

organiser.title: People
organiser.body: Everyone who signed up. Add sign-up questions, approve applications if you want to check people first, and invite co-organisers.

organiser.title: Teams
organiser.body: Teams as they form. Set the team size, turn team finding on or off, and place people who are still on no team.

organiser.title: Entries
organiser.body: What each team submitted. Set the deadline, choose which fields are required, and give one team more time.

organiser.title: Judging
organiser.body: Write the scoring rubric, choose how judges get their teams, watch progress, and lock judging when every score is in.

organiser.title: Results
organiser.body: Preview the standings, publish them, and choose what the public sees. People’s choice voting and the directory listing are here too.

organiser.title: Settings
organiser.body: Your organiser details, website notifications, and deleting the event.

organiser.title: Any time
organiser.body: Open this walkthrough again from Help. You can also run every step from an AI app if you prefer.

judge.title: Thank you for judging
judge.body: Here is how it works. It takes about 30 seconds.

judge.title: Is scoring open?
judge.body: This tells you whether you can score. Scoring opens when entries close, and ends when the organiser locks it.

judge.title: Start here
judge.body: This button opens the next team you have not scored yet. When every team is scored, it says you are done.

judge.title: Your progress
judge.body: How many of your teams you have scored so far.

judge.title: My teams
judge.body: Every team you are scoring. Scored teams move to Scored. Teams where you know someone go under Teams I know.

judge.title: Rubric & brief
judge.body: What each criterion means and what the points are for. Read it once before you start.

judge.title: Scoring a team
judge.body: Open the team’s website, then tap a score for each criterion. Every tap saves straight away, there is no Save button. Add a comment if you like, then Save & next.

judge.title: If you know someone on a team
judge.body: Press I know someone on this team. The team leaves your list and your score for it stops counting. You can undo it from My teams.

judge.title: Any time
judge.body: Open this walkthrough again from Help.

decisions.q: Does a conflicted judge's earlier score still count toward the team's computed result?

states.shows: HTTP 410 and noindex as today. Plain page: top bar, the title, 'This event has been taken down.', the reason when given, 'Find another hackathon'. No icon, no event colour (brand red), no content, no link-preview image. Also replaces a custom website.

states.name: empty organiser content
states.shows: The section and its chip are left out. No empty headings. If About, Tracks, Prizes, Schedule, Rules, FAQ and Sponsors are all empty, the page is the header and the stage card.

public_pages.custom_website: Unchanged. When the organiser switches the event address to their own uploaded site, <event>.simple-hack.app serves that site and this built-in page stays reachable at simple-hack.app/e/<slug>, which is the stable, trusted copy (same template, same data). Join, judge and vote links always go to simple-hack.app, so they work with either mode. A take-down overrides the custom site and shows the taken-down state above. The redesign touches only the built-in page.
tech_notes: Server-rendered from the existing hackEventView. Every section works without JavaScript. Jump chips are plain anchor links, older announcements, FAQ, collapsed Schedule and Rules use details/summary.
One script stays, the nonce-carrying countdown, and it only rewrites the time-left text. No inline handlers.

Uses the app kit (AppURL/hack/kit.css, CSP already allows style-src from AppURL) plus a few page rules inline. Drops the site header, hack-ink.css and the theme switch (light only). Keeps the shared footer links.

Event colour: --ev is the organiser's colour for the header rule, stage card border, icon fallback and letter marks. --accent for buttons and links is color-mix(in srgb, --ev 50%, #000), the same AA rule hack-ink.css uses today, declared after a plain brand-red fallback so old Android browsers without color-mix still get a readable accent.

Head: title '<Title> · Simple Hack', meta description and og:description = tagline (fallback: stage words), og:title, og:type website, og:image = IconURL (not when taken down), twitter:card summary. noindex for draft and taken down as today.
Speed on a cheap phone: system fonts, no web fonts, screenshots lazy-loaded with width and height set, kit.css cached from the app origin.
fixes: Hand-drawn ink look, tilted cards and a dark-mode switch replaced by the app kit's calm straight style, light only, still themed by the event colour and icon.

Open stage: today's only join guidance is a grey pill 'Sign-up is open. Ask the organisers for the join link.' (atlas: 'a visitor ... has no way to act on this page'). Now a stage card explains how joining works and gives people who already joined a way in. A real Join button needs data the page does not have (feature idea 1).
'Anyone can join. No coding needed.' was shown on every open or building event, also on approval-only ones. Removed, the organiser's own About and FAQ say who can join.
Results sat at the very bottom after eight sections. They now come first in Results and Ended.
The team gallery sat last. It now follows the stage card from Closed on, and has a count and one link per card.
The deadline countdown kept running in Results ('Entries are closed.'). Time left now shows only in Open and Building, a static closing time in Closed, nothing after.
Announcement dates were UTC days. They now use the event's time zone, like every other time on the page.
Multi-day schedule items showed only the end time ('Wed 28 Oct, 10:00–18:00'). The end date is shown when it is a different day.
The date line showed the zone as 'Asia/Jakarta'. It now says 'times in WIB'.
Scores read '80.00 (raw)' on every row. The method is said once above the list in plain words.
Link previews: today only og:image is set. Adds title, description and card tags so a WhatsApp or Instagram share shows the event name and tagline.
The phone page was over 3,300px with no way to jump. Adds 'On this page' chips, collapses Rules and Schedule after the event and folds older announcements.
Tracks were near the bottom. Prospects see them right after About.
'Visit sponsor' links all had the same name. Each now says 'Visit <sponsor>'.
Taken down keeps the 410 and the reason, drops the event colour and adds a way out (Find another hackathon).
Corrects the previous atlas entry, which promised status tags on gallery cards and a 'results expected' date. Neither exists in the data, both moved to feature ideas.
public_pages.phone: Same order as desktop, one column, 16px gutter. Icon sits above the title, facts on short separate lines, chips scroll sideways, stage card button is full width, Team sites are compact rows with a small thumbnail, Schedule times sit under titles, every tap target is at least 44px. No sticky bars.

decisions.q: What is the main action in Open when the page cannot show the join link?
decisions.decision: A stage card titled 'Join with the link from the organisers' that says where the link usually comes from, plus a quiet 'Already joined? Sign in'. No fake Join button.
decisions.why: The view has no join URL and the app has no way to type a join code, so a button would lead nowhere. Telling a first-timer exactly what to look for is the honest next step. Showing the link is feature idea 1 for the owner.

decisions.q: One page order for all stages, or reorder by stage?
decisions.decision: Reorder by stage. The header and footer never move, the block under the header is the stage's job, and sections follow who reads the page at that stage.
decisions.why: The readers change completely: prospects and parents before, participants during, everyone looking for winners after. One fixed order buries results under eight sections, which is today's main complaint.

decisions.q: Where does 'Sign in' / 'Already joined' go?
decisions.decision: AppURL/events (Your events), not /e/<slug>/team.
decisions.why: The page cannot know the reader's role. /e/<slug>/team renders participant screens even for a judge or organiser, while Your events works for every role and returns there after sign-in.

decisions.q: Who sees the organiser identity?
decisions.decision: 'Organised by Amara Putri (Generation Girl)' sits in the header facts line on every stage, and the footer keeps Report a page.
decisions.why: A parent or teacher decides legitimacy from who runs it. Today the line is small and grey under the title.

decisions.q: What happens to sections that matter less after the event?
decisions.decision: Schedule and Rules collapse into details in Results and Ended. Nothing is removed.
decisions.why: Reorganise, do not remove. Collapsing keeps the content reachable without making the results page long on a phone.

decisions.q: Status tags on gallery cards?
decisions.decision: No tags. Cards show screenshot or letter, title, tagline, team name and one link.
decisions.why: The card data has no per-team status. The stage card and stage pill already say what is happening to every team.

decisions.q: How does the event colour theme the page without breaking contrast?
decisions.decision: Raw colour for rules, borders, letter marks and the icon fallback. A 50%-darkened mix for buttons and links, with brand red as fallback.
decisions.why: Some crayons (yellow, orange) fail as text or button colour on paper. This is the same rule the ink page uses today, so organisers see the same identity.

decisions.q: Keep the countdown?
decisions.decision: Yes, only in Open and Building, as the one nonce script. Without JavaScript the closing date and time is shown.
decisions.why: Participants mid-event want time left at a glance. The date alone is complete without the script.

decisions.q: Header nav like the app shell?
decisions.decision: No shell. A plain top bar with the wordmark, Find a hackathon and Sign in.
decisions.why: Owner direction 7: public pages stay pages. Visitors have no role and no event switcher.

decisions.q: Should Team sites show in the open stage too?
decisions.decision: Team sites show from sign-up when the gallery is on, as before (review 2026-10-30)
decisions.why: The old page showed the gallery in every stage after draft whenever the gallery switch was on, and voting can open before entries close too. layout_by_stage.open had dropped it; restored right after Tracks, the same adjacency every later stage keeps between the two.

feature_ideas: 1. Show a Join button on the public page (organiser opt-in that exposes the join link). Today the page cannot show it, and the app has no field to type a join code.
2. An approval-required flag in the page data, so Open can say 'The organisers review every sign-up'.

3. Where and for whom: a format/location field (Online, or a venue and city) and an eligibility line (age, who can join). Parents look for both, today they only exist if the organiser writes them into About.
4. An organiser contact (email) for questions from parents, sponsors and judges.
5. The code of conduct on the public page. It is shown on the join page but not in the event page data.
6. A 'results expected' date for the Judging stage, and the results published time.
7. Voting open and close times, so People's choice can say 'Voting opens Fri 30 Oct, 09:00 WIB'.
8. Track name on gallery cards (the card data has no track).
9. A has-uploaded-icon flag, so link previews can fall back to a PNG. The automatic icon is an SVG, which WhatsApp does not show as a preview image.
10. Small screenshot thumbnails for the gallery (screenshots can be up to 2 MB each) and sponsor logos served as cached files instead of data URIs inside the HTML (up to 128 KB each).
11. A role-aware link such as simple-hack.app/e/<slug>/open that sends a signed-in member straight to their own Home in the event.
open_questions: Is keeping the join link off the public page deliberate (only people the organiser sends it to can join)? If yes, the Open stage card stays as designed. If no, feature idea 1 becomes the Open stage's main action.
OK to drop 'Anyone can join. No coding needed.' from the header? It is wrong for approval-only events and for events that do need code.
Draft: keep showing the organiser's full content (it is their only preview, and noindex) with a 'Not open yet' card, or hide everything but the title?

Plain wording for the score method line: what should 'raw' and 'normalised' say to a parent? Proposed: 'Scores are the judges' average' and 'Scores are adjusted so strict and generous judges count the same'.
Should the team and participant counts show during Open? They are reassuring for a big event and off-putting for a new one with 3 sign-ups.

planned.name: Leave this event
planned.what: Any participant, judge or organiser can leave an event they joined. A participant leaves their team first. A judge's scores are kept. The event creator hands the event to another organiser first. The last organiser is told nobody would be left to run it, so leaving closes it: End the event or Delete the event, or Cancel.
